subject: Private VPC — renewal + satellite capacity proposal
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Lina Zhou <lina.zhou@hearthlabs.com>, HearthLabs Procurement <procurement@hearthlabs.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private VPC — renewal + satellite capacity proposal

Hi Lina / team,

Happy to follow up on our renewal conversation. Based on the usage telemetry over the last 12 months and your expansion ask for analytics workloads in EWR and SJC, we've put together two options for how to handle the Private deployment at renewal:

1) Phased satellite rollout (recommended) — 36-month term, primary VPC in us-east-1, two satellite clusters (sfo + nyc) configured for cold-failover and KV prefix caching. Minimal downtime cutover window: 6 hours.
2) Immediate multi-cluster cutover — 24-month term, full active-active across three clusters, higher baseline cost but lower tail latency for geo-split requests.

Attached: SOW_hearthlabs_private_vpc_v1.pdf (SOW draft), pricing_options_202712.xlsx (line-item pricing and term comparisons), capacity_runbook_20271214.xlsx (initial capacity forecast).

Questions for you to confirm so we can finalize an amendment and push to DocuSign:
- Preferred term (24 vs 36 months)
- Target go-live quarter (Q1 2028 preferred by your team?)
- Any residency or audit constraints for the satellite sites (e.g., data residency lock, additional audit logging)?

If easiest, propose a short 30-min call Thurs to walk pricing and cutover plan.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0187

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference for teams
From: Lina Zhou <lina.zhou@hearthlabs.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: HearthLabs IT <it@hearthlabs.com>, HearthLabs Procurement <procurement@hearthlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC — renewal + satellite capacity proposal

Thanks Rafael — appreciate the clear options. A few quick clarifications before we book time: 

- Data residency: the analytics cluster in SJC will process PHI-adjacent telemetry; we need the satellite site to support our retention controls and immutable audit logs. Can you confirm that the satellite cluster supports per-tenant retention policies and KMS integration?
- SOC2 documentation: procurement needs the latest SOC2 Type II report and a short summary of network segmentation controls to attach to the PO.
- Pricing question: is there a stepped discount for committed burst capacity in Q1 (we expect a 30% spike for a 6-week migration window)?

If those answers look good, procurement is prepared to sign an amendment. Proposed timeline: sign in Jan 2028, phased rollout in Feb–Mar 2028.

Lina
Lina Zhou
Head of Infrastructure | HearthLabs
lina.zhou@hearthlabs.com

Rafael / team — quick technical notes to include in the amendment and SOW: 

- Retention/KMS: Private runtime supports per-tenant retention windows via per-namespace policies. We can bind customer keys via AWS KMS or bring-your-own-HSM; will note required IAM roles and key rotation cadence in the SOW.
- Auditing: system audit logs can be exported to your S3 bucket (read-only) and we can enable immutable logs for the satellite clusters.
- Phased approach cutover: recommend a blue/green prefix routing for the analytics workload to avoid an application-level outage. Typical database sync window: 4–8 hours depending on backfill size.
- Capacity notes: the attached deployment_phased_plan.md (excerpt) shows a 20% buffer for burst and suggested auto-scaling policies.

I'll attach the deployment_phased_plan.md and a 1-page technical summary for procurement.

—Ben
